keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; Later Mayan City-States begins 850). The page gives 'some 80 km2' built up and 'some 50,000 inhabitants' but no kingdom extent; 'a vast area' is drawn as a 60 km disc (about 11,000 km2), soft.

ledger.note: 201: 'Between 201 and 601 AD, Coba must have dominated a vast area'; 'Cobá was first settled between 50 BC and 100 AD' and grew strongly 'after 100 AD'. The page gives no founding of a state.

ledger.note: After 600: 'the emergence of powerful city states of the Puuc culture' (page); the page gives no date for any particular loss, so 601 (the end of the 201-601 span) is a bridge. Reviewer am-02: region narrowed to the ring the 601 keyframe drops (the whole 60 km disc removed the core too), counterpart set to nobody (the page has the Puuc cities 'eroding the dominance' of Cobá, not taking its land).

ledger.note: About 950: 'Beginning around 900 or 1000 AD' Cobá declines, 'with the latter [Chichen Itza] dominating at the end as it gained control of key cities such as Yaxuná'; Cobá was reoccupied 'from 1200-1500 AD' and 'abandoned by the time the Spanish conquered the peninsula'. Bridge date.

sources.title: Coba
sources.note: Settled 50 BC-100 AD; 'Between 201 and 601 AD, Coba must have dominated a vast area'; Puuc city-states after 600; Chichen Itza dominating at the end; 80 km2 built up; Yaxuna sacbe.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Cobá row. The page's dates are loose: 'first settled between 50 BC and 100 AD', 'Between 201 and 601 AD ... dominated a vast area', Late Classic 600-900, decline 'around 900 or 1000'; several carry 'citation needed'. The page names a ruling woman Yopaat 'who ruled Cobá between 500 and 780 AD' (no ruler strip). The infobox gives 20°29′24″N 87°43′55″W and the body text 19°29.6'N 87°43.7'W; the infobox matches the gazetteer.
COUNTERPARTS. Yaxuná (the end of the long sacbe, 'almost 100 km') and the Puuc city-states have no dossiers; Uxmal is a thin dossier in this batch.
